title: 7075, 7050, and 6061 in Defense: Alloy Selection for DoD Programs
summary: Compare 6061, 7075 and 7050 plate by specified temper, manufacturing process, material documentation and the requirements of the defense order.
body_markdown:
## 6061 for fabrication and machined parts


6061 is widely used for fixtures, housings and fabricated parts whose requirements it meets. Conventional arc welding is a common fabrication option, but welding changes properties near the joint. The original plate strength does not automatically carry into a welded assembly.


[Shop 6061 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/6061-aluminum)[Kaiser: 6061 technical data](https://online.kaiseraluminum.com/depot/PublicProductInformation/Document/1015/Kaiser_Aluminum_6061_Sheet_Coil_and_Plate.pdf)


## 7075: compare the specified temper


7075 plate is used for high-strength applications. T651 and overaged T7351 offer different strength and stress-corrosion behavior. Order the specified temper and evaluate the required thickness and test direction rather than assigning one strength value to every 7075 plate.


[Shop 7075 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/7075-aluminum)[Kaiser: 7075 technical data](https://online.kaiseraluminum.com/depot/PublicProductInformation/Document/1017/Kaiser_Aluminum_7075_Sheet_Coil_and_Plate.pdf)


## 7050 for thick-section performance


7050 has lower quench sensitivity than many other high-strength aluminum alloys, making it useful in thick aerospace plate. T7451 and T7651 are distinct overaged, stress-relieved tempers. AMS 4050 covers T7451 plate; AMS 4201 covers T7651 plate. There is no universal plate thickness that requires switching from 7075 to 7050.


[Shop 7050 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/7050-aluminum)[Kaiser: 7050 technical data](https://online.kaiseraluminum.com/depot/PublicProductInformation/Document/1016/Kaiser_Aluminum_7050_Sheet_Coil_and_Plate.pdf)[SAE: AMS 4050](https://doi.org/10.4271/AMS4050K)[SAE: AMS 4201](https://doi.org/10.4271/AMS4201H)


## Keep reference properties separate from acceptance requirements


Manufacturer typical properties help explain differences between materials. They are not specification minima or design allowables. Use approved engineering data for design and the governing product specification, thickness and test direction for material acceptance.


## Apply the actual order’s source requirements


Ordinary aluminum alloys such as 6061, 7075 and 7050 are not within the specialty-metal definition in DFARS 252.225-7009. Aluminum appears there as an alloying element in certain steels, not as a category of aluminum plate. A purchase order can still impose separate origin, domestic-melt, material or documentation requirements.


[DFARS 7009: scope and rules](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7009-restriction-acquisition-certain-articles-containing-specialty-metals.)[Origin and mill certificates](https://noxmetals.co/services/dfars-compliance)


## Check the current offer and substitution requirements


Request a current price and delivery estimate for the exact cut, quantity and documentation. Fixed alloy price multiples and universal lead-time charts do not establish what a supplier can deliver today. Obtain the required engineering and purchasing approvals before changing the alloy, temper or source.
